hypotheses.reasoning: The alert (POST /v1/notify 503s) is a downstream symptom. The origin is in notification-svc: a rollout of v3.13.0 with config revision 645 (#236), then at #243 the live config reload changed TEMPLATE_SVC_URL to http://template-svc.internal:8081. Immediately after, notification-svc's TemplateClient.render fails with connect ECONNREFUSED 10.17.189.215:8081 (#248, repeated #256, #258, #271). Before the reload, template-svc was rendering fine (#238 m-3143 ok). After the reload, template-svc logs no /render calls at all, even though notification-svc accepted m-3146 (#241) and m-3147 (#244) and tried to call it. template-svc is still alive (GC debug lines continue through 13:32), so it is not crashing; the notification-svc is simply sending to an endpoint that refuses connections. Gateway 503s (#251 onward) are the downstream effect and are not cited as causes. The deploy at #236 is a confounder, but the failures begin at the config key change, not at the binary rollout, which points to a bad config value. Ruled out: template-svc resource exhaustion (only normal GC pauses), notif-db (only a slow audit query, no errors), redis (no errors), and the single email-provider retry at #64 (recovered).

Alternative reading: the notification-svc v3.13.0 rollout (build 1816aca) happened at #236, shortly before failures began. But the logs show the rollout completed without errors and that the failures start with the config reload (#243) followed by ECONNREFUSED on the new URL, so the release alone does not explain it. A rollback would also clear the bad config, so it is a plausible remediation path.

verdict.recommendedAction: Revert notification-svc's TEMPLATE_SVC_URL to the previous value (the one in effect before config revision 645) or correct the endpoint so it actually reaches template-svc (confirm where template-svc listens; it is serving normally). Roll back config revision 645 in config-service, or roll back notification-svc to the prior release if the config cannot be reverted quickly. Then confirm /render calls resume in template-svc and the gateway success rate recovers. Follow up by adding config validation (health-check the new endpoint before applying a reload) and alerting on TemplateClient connection refused.

hypotheses.reasoning: The alert (POST /v1/notify 503s) is a downstream symptom. The origin is in notification-svc: a rollout of v3.13.0 with config revision 645 (#236), then at #243 the live config reload changed TEMPLATE_SVC_URL to http://template-svc.internal:8081. Immediately after, notification-svc's TemplateClient.render fails with connect ECONNREFUSED 10.17.189.215:8081 (#248, repeated #256, #258, #271). Before the reload, template-svc was rendering fine (#238 m-3143 ok). After the reload, template-svc logs no /render calls at all, even though notification-svc accepted m-3146 (#241) and m-3147 (#244) and tried to call it. template-svc is still alive (GC debug lines continue through 13:32), so it is not crashing; the notification-svc is simply sending to an endpoint that refuses connections. Gateway 503s (#251 onward) are the downstream effect and are not cited as causes. The deploy at #236 is a confounder, but the failures begin at the config key change, not at the binary rollout, which points to a bad config value. Ruled out: template-svc resource exhaustion (only normal GC pauses), notif-db (only a slow audit query, no errors), redis (no errors), and the single email-provider retry at #64 (recovered).

Alternative reading: the notification-svc v3.13.0 rollout (build 1816aca) happened at #236, shortly before failures began. But the logs show the rollout completed without errors and that the failures start with the config reload (#243) followed by ECONNREFUSED on the new URL, so the release alone does not explain it. A rollback would also clear the bad config, so it is a plausible remediation path.
